subject: Differential discount structure + batching/cache/quant recommendations

Cc: procurement@dataforge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Optimize Toolkit — pricing structure and technical recommendations request

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — DataForge is keen to move from PoC to a 6-week pilot for our document ingestion + question-answering pipeline. A couple of asks from our side before we lock timing:

- We need a clear commercial model for the pilot: what discounts or credits are available for experimental pilots vs. production commitments?
- Can you recommend quantization and batching knobs for our workload? Typical prompt lengths average 450 tokens and 98% of requests are under 1k tokens; embeddings used for retrieval.
- We’re worried about token costs for re-processing old documents; is there an efficient KV/prefix cache option?

We have a procurement lead in cc who wants rough pricing numbers to prepare a PO.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of ML, DataForge

(Procurement contact: procurement@dataforge.ai)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, procurement@dataforge.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — pricing structure and technical recommendations request

Hi Priya — great to hear you want to move forward. Quick answers, then I’ll loop in Marcus and Evelyn for detail.

1) Pilot economics: we typically offer a three-part structure for pilots:
   - Pilot credit package (timeboxed credits against hosted API usage)
   - Conditional production discount if you convert to a committed monthly band within 60 days
   - A one-time onboarding credit for engineering support

I’ve attached a short pricing table with suggested bands (redwood-optimize-pricing-table.xlsx). Marcus — can you propose concrete numbers and a short MOU?

2) Quantization / batching guidance: Evelyn — could you confirm recommended quant levels for DataForge’s token distribution? My initial read: 8-bit quantization (qat/int8) for generation models should be safe for retrieval-augmented generation; consider 4-bit for cost pressure but validate quality on your eval set. For batching, start with a target latency SLO of 350ms p50 and allow batching up to 16 for background inference; for interactive lower-latency routes keep batch size 1–4.

3) KV cache / prefixing: our Optimize toolkit supports request-level prefix caching with TTL. For your use case (re-processing historical documents), we recommend a warmed-on-demand cache with TTL of 6–12 hours and a prefetch policy on frequent queries. Evelyn will add specifics.

I’ll get a short commercial proposal and pilot SOW over today.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Priya — Dylan summarized well. A practical commercial proposal to fast-track the pilot:

- Pilot credit: $25k USD hosted credits (covers estimated tokens for 6-week pilot based on provided distribution).
- Conversion incentive: if DataForge signs a 12-month committed capacity (>= $200k ARR) within 60 days after pilot, we’ll apply a 25% rebate credited back as service credits pro-rata for the first quarter.
- Proof-of-concept discount: 15% off standard generation rates during pilot (applied on top of credits).
- Technical onboarding: 8 hours of engineering support (included); additional hours billed at standard SE rate.

Attached is a short MOU / pilot MOP template (pilot-mop-template.docx) — it captures success criteria and acceptance testing. If procurement is comfortable, we can take a PO for the pilot credits and I’ll route paper for signature.

Notes on risk: the conversion incentive is timebound and requires minimal SLA expectations (we’ll include a 99.5% regional availability target for pilot endpoints).

Marcus
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@dataforge.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Priya — quick technical checklist and recommended knobs for your evaluation set:

- Model choice: for RAG I’d recommend a 30B open variant we’ve verified in Optimize for stable QA accuracy when quantized.
- Quantization:
  * Start with dynamic 8-bit (INT8) quant on the 30B model. Run a small eval (1k prompts) to compare F1/QA accuracy vs fp16 baseline.
  * If cost needs further reduction, test 4-bit (QLoRA-style) on a shadow subset; expect ~2–4% drop in answer fidelity for some prompt types.
- Batching: set a dual-route strategy — interactive (p50 < 350ms, batch 1–4, pre-warm KV) and background (throughput jobs, batch up to 32).
- KV cache: recommendations for your workload:
  * Use per-document prefix keys with an LRU + TTL of 6 hours for recency-sensitive flows.
  * Enable prefetch for top 50 frequent queries per hour to avoid cold-starts.
  * Cache compression: store compressed KV slices to reduce memory footprint; Optimize supports LZ4 for speedy decompress.
- Token accounting: enable token-cost reporting per-route in Console to identify re-process heavy routes (we’ve seen customers save 18–27% after excluding cold reprocessing).

Attached is a short KV guide (kv-cache-guidance.pdf) showing our recommended prefetch config and a sample eval script. Happy to run a joint eval (we can run a 1k prompt validation and share metrics).

—Evelyn
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Procurement asked me to confirm two items before I share to legal:

1) The pilot credit package is purchasable via PO and will be applied to hosted usage automatically (we don’t need a separate commercial appendix), correct?
2) The conversion incentive (25% rebate) — can it be captured in a short MOU with milestone language (pilot acceptance -> PO conversion within 60 days)?

If both answers are yes we’ll prepare a PO for the $25k pilot credits and return a signed MOU — legal typically needs the link to the HubSpot deal and the pilot MOP.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Priya
Head of ML, DataForge
